text:
Astra is the working name for a pre–Genesis Pin layer: global relational consistency as a quantum-information law that would sit before identity, hashing, and ordered history. The 5 Sep gloss is a question. The 5–6 Sep identities are finite exact results in a controlled family. They are not Origin Law, not a gravity law, and not the pin. Stop-rule: if this week grows another exact identity, append it here. Do not fork a fourth gravity page.

New finite consistency identities this week append to this article. Emergent gravity stays the candidate-gravity gloss. Genesis Pin stays legitimacy. Causal stack stays retained closures. The September 2026 v13 campaign (QRSL / HCPR / QMAR) lives on the live board — GitHub-only, not a fourth gravity page.

The question (Open)

Gravity may not be the fundamental law. It may inherit its universality from a deeper quantum law that governs global relational consistency.

Posted as a pre–Genesis Pin extension of the information layer. Mathematics in-thread suggested it was possible. Gravity was not claimed then and is not claimed now.

Finite consistency family (Restricted)

The same week produced three exact identities in a controlled finite model. Global consistency fixes the numbers. No fitted response law. Continuum identification of the response with curvature or Einstein is still required before any gravity reading.

F\le\frac{k+1}{2k}

For one qubit with k partners and equal pair states: F ≤ (k+1)/(2k). Global consistency forces this bound — no fitted response law. The gravity connection remains open.

7–10 Sep: from source scan to a closed algebra

The Astra question did not freeze on 6 Sep. Four posts later that week moved from a reconstructible source map, to a conditional universal source coefficient, to a continuum normalization of an N-cycle inverse, to an explicit qubit constraint algebra with a public 121-step simulation. Gravity’s constraints are still not identified. The stop-rule holds: the identities append here; the simulation packet has its own article so the MP4, CSV, and Python can be run.
